solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: How Red revolt goes wrong everywhere on earth

indicators.note: a revolt that goes wrong falls apart, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A failed communist uprising is collapsing in every country at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' looks like a communist, but it is just three letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning in every part of the globe, all around the planet.

clue.text: The female element evident in plant collection

parts.note: her is the female pronoun
barium is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A female chemist spots some element in a botanist's collection of specimens.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbarium is an organised collection of dried, pressed botanical specimens kept for study.

clue.text: Desire to grow old in Oxon town

parts.note: to desire is to want
to age is to grow old

explanation.surface: Someone longs to retire to a quiet town in Oxfordshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxon is the abbreviation for Oxfordshire, an English county west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantage is a market town in the Vale of White Horse, historically in Berkshire, now Oxfordshire.

clue.text: Spin rubbish at end of conference

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of conference

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A delegate dismisses the spin put about at the close of a conference as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' reads as political spin, but it is the verb meaning turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn about an axis, the same motion as a spinning top.

clue.text: Very small daughter fighting loudly

parts.note: fighting on a large scale is war
F, forte, is the musical direction meaning loudly

explanation.surface: A tiny girl is quarrelling at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word describes something far below normal size, a miniature or stunted version.

clue.text: Cleaner's short holiday

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short for a vacuum cleaner
second meaning: short for vacation, especially a university vacation

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive, as if a cleaner were taking a break; it is just 'is' joining two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a vacuum cleaner and a university vacation are colloquially abbreviated to the same three letters.

clue.text: Army corps with lack of communication, one bound to be showing adaptability

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: something bound is tied up and held, so one sits enclosed within the word for quiet

parts.note: silence is an absence of speech
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An army unit that never talks to each other still somehow copes flexibly.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers; 'bound' reads as obliged, but here it means tied in, holding one within the quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Resilience is the capacity to recover and adjust when conditions change, close to flexibility.

clue.text: Little bird making fresh journey back across river

indicators.note: the word straddles the river letter, which ends up within it
a journey back runs in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: fresh means new
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A small bird sets off again, flying home over a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journey back' turns NEW into WEN, and 'across' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wren is one of the tiniest common European songbirds, brown with a cocked tail.

clue.text: What can suggest certain psychological states? Disturbed rest can

indicators.note: a disturbed rest is broken up, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A sleeper whose rest is interrupted might show signs of odd mental conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance is a half-conscious, dreamlike condition, as under hypnosis.

clue.text: Flying yet to be decided upon?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that a flight might still be undecided; really the phrase has a literal and a figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means airborne; figuratively it describes plans still unresolved.

clue.text: Vegetables obtained by worker, a lowly labourer

parts.note: peas are vegetables
a worker is a type of ant, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A humble farmhand is paid in vegetables by his employer.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor agricultural worker of low social rank, toiling on the land.

clue.text: Wild female, real crazy

indicators.note: crazy suggests something out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A slangy exclamation about a woman who has gone truly mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feral describes an animal that has reverted to an untamed state from domestication.

clue.text: It's a loner disturbing members of the family

indicators.note: disturbing something throws it into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary person upsetting their kin at a family gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations are relatives, people connected by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Any number were ill and had a seizure?

definitions.note: a verb phrase in the past tense, matching the past-tense answer

parts.note: N stands for an unspecified number in maths
ailed means were unwell

explanation.surface: Asking whether a crowd of sick people had a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seizure' suggests a medical fit; here it means a capture, as police nail a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To nail someone is informally to catch or arrest them, i.e. to seize them.

clue.text: Lover I betrayed — conclusion of romance

parts.note: to sell someone out is to betray them, so betrayed is sold

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, here of romance

parts.note: its final letter

explanation.surface: A jilted partner laments being deceived at the end of an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Isolde is the Irish princess of the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the famous beloved of Tristan in medieval legend, a tragic lover.

clue.text: Austere Pole with evidence of sunbathing

parts.note: a spar is a pole, as on a ship
a tan is the browning of skin left by sunbathing

explanation.surface: A stern Polish man shows off his suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is capitalised to look like a Polish person; it is a wooden pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means severely simple and frugal, after the disciplined ancient Spartans.

clue.text: Notice academic fellow's extra items

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
a don is a university fellow; with the 's it gives DONS

explanation.surface: A notice belonging to a college fellow lists some additional things.
explanation.definitionFit: Add-ons are supplementary components or features attached to something basic.

clue.text: Famous writer's sporting run

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ancient Greek epic poet of the Iliad and Odyssey
second meaning: a home run in baseball

explanation.walkthrough: The 's looks possessive but is 'is', linking two meanings; a homer is a baseball home run.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the Greek epic poet and, uncapitalised, to a baseball home run.

clue.text: Exceptionally large and majestic

indicators.note: exceptionally suggests an unusual form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something grand and stately is of remarkable size.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal means kingly, fit for royalty, hence stately and grand.

clue.text: Doctor, when facing twitching, is severe

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a tic is an involuntary twitching

explanation.surface: A doctor confronting a patient's spasms judges the case serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Drastic means extreme or harsh in effect, like severe measures.

clue.text: Everyone wanting ogre destroyed quickly

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: a destroyed thing is broken apart, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The whole village wants a monster killed fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Allegro is the musical tempo marking for a brisk pace.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the Italian term directs players to perform at a lively, fast tempo.

clue.text: Fate of item put up for sale

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one's ... in life, destiny

explanation.walkthrough: The 'of' seems to make one phrase about an item's fate; it just joins two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means one's destiny in life and also a numbered item offered at auction.

clue.text: Old English character, almost a god

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the thorn is an Old English letter, written as a p-like rune for TH

explanation.surface: An old Anglo-Saxon fellow is nearly divine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old English character' sounds like a person, but it is the runic letter thorn.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse thunder deity who wields a hammer.

clue.text: Cruelty of situation after baseball Babe had retired?

indicators.note: the state word comes after the rest, at the end

parts.note: Babe Ruth was a famous American baseball player
once he had retired the game was without him, Ruth-less
the suffix -ness denotes a state or condition

explanation.surface: Baseball lamenting how it was once Babe Ruth had quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whimsically: the state of things once Ruth left is RUTH-LESS-NESS. Babe Ruth was a legendary US baseball star.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruthlessness means having no pity or compassion, hence cruelty.
